Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging on second person pronouns?

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging on full NPs?

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the imperfective aspect?

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the perfective aspect?

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the past tense?
Comment: The ergative alignment system is consistently applied in clauses that refer to past events. It does not morphologically distinguish between past and present tense, but rather uses a broader category called "commended tense," which encompasses both.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in non-past tenses?
Comment: The ergative-absolutive alignment remains solidly in times past.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the indicative mood?

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the context of an agentive A?
Comment: When argument A is a prototypical agent (volitional, initiating and controlling the action), it is consistently marked with the ergative case, while P and S are marked with the absolutive (trigger) case.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the context of a non-agentive A?
Comment: Ergative alignment is maintained even when argument A is not a prototypical agent, as in the case of experiencers of perception or psychological verbs.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the context of a topical A?
Comment: The "topic" argument is the argument that is in the absolutive case (called the "trigger case"). Argument A is always in the non-absolutive (ergative) case.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the context of a non-topical A?
Comment: All arguments A (marked with ergative case) in transitive clauses are non-topic (or non-trigger).

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the context of an animate A?
